items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6wy: Ukraine's President Zelensky called the strikes on the Crimean Bridge a 'fair response' to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges inside Ukraine, saying Putin wants an excuse to escalate, not to stop. He rejected Russia's claim the bridge is purely civilian, citing images of tanks resupplying occupied Crimea across it, even as the bridge faces repeated drone and missile strikes.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/2: Hundreds of displaced Palestinians near Gaza's 'Yellow Line' protested after Israeli forces destroyed more than 500 housing units in under a month, beyond the line Israel withdrew to under last year's ceasefire. A local mayor called it a policy of 'gradual creeping displacement' meant to force residents out, while Gaza's housing ministry says 350,000 families are now homeless, with recent flooding also destroying tent camps.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026: Multiple coastal hazard warnings hit California this week as Pacific storms produced waves over 30ft, with a Monterey buoy recording 34.1ft, potentially the highest in 30 years. Beaches and piers closed as swells of 10-22ft were expected through the week, while the same storm systems brought record rainfall to San Francisco and knocked out power for 32,000 Sacramento customers.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj75: A Russian cargo ship, the Sparta II, bound for Kaliningrad was hit by a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland and caught fire before drifting into Finnish waters; Finnish authorities say Ukraine was likely responsible. The sanctioned vessel is linked to Russia's defence ministry, and Finland's PM said Ukraine has the right to fight back, while Kaliningrad's governor said there was no threat to the region's supplies.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he's still living on a US military base, two weeks after an Israeli warning over Iran sent him into hiding, the second such warning to force a top US official into extraordinary security measures.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/environment/: Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old, 20-tonne baobab trees after an exporter dug them up without permits to ship them to an unnamed buyer in Georgia. Intercepted in Durban in July, the trees have reached a Timbavati reserve to be replanted and cabled for support, echoing a similar case in Kenya where baobabs were sent to a park owned by a Georgian billionaire.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6ly: UN climate talks (COP31) in Turkey are deadlocked and suspended after running over a day late, with nearly 200 countries unable to agree on a new deal. The EU and Pacific nations oppose a draft with no mention of cutting fossil-fuel demand, while the Africa Group wants more adaptation funding the EU won't support, raising the chance of a rare no-deal outcome, last seen only once since 1995.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Video showed moviegoers fleeing a cinema screening the new Hunger Games film when a 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck Peru on Friday.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/global-devel: A UN report finds one in four women globally cannot refuse sex with their husband or partner, with nearly half of women in west and central Africa unable to say no, and a third in east/southern Africa and Arab states facing the same. Younger women aged 15-19 have even less power to refuse than older women, and the findings align with high rates of intimate partner violence against adolescent girls.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckz7: Fausto Isidro 'Chapo Isidro' Meza Flores, on the FBI's 10 most-wanted list for allegedly trafficking fentanyl, cocaine and heroin into the US, was arrested after a shoot-out with Mexican special forces in Sinaloa that killed seven suspects and four soldiers. The Guasave Cartel leader had evaded capture since the 1990s by keeping a low profile; the US is now seeking his extradition amid Mexico's intensified crackdown on cartels under pressure from President Trump.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/r: At least nine people, all from one family, were killed and several injured when a vehicle carrying 16 pilgrims returning to Maharashtra from Khatu Shyam rammed a parked truck on the Kota-Udaipur highway in Rajasthan, police said. Officials said the administration's immediate priority was ensuring medical treatment for the injured.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/can-jail: Jailed Punjab MP Amritpal Singh made his first physical appearance in Punjab since his 2023 arrest, a 3-hour visit seen as a possible boost for his Waris Punjab De party ahead of Punjab's assembly polls.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: PM Modi told graduates of a Uttar Pradesh skilling programme in Lucknow that India's trained technicians, not just degree holders, would protect jobs from AI, as the state's Skill Development Mission has trained over 1.7 million people and placed more than 700,000 since 2017. He announced UP will host the World Skills Asia competition in 2027 and cited local semiconductor and BrahMos missile projects, months ahead of the state's assembly elections.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Coi: Tamil Nadu, with 10,000-11,000 MW of installed solar capacity, may see installations slow in 2027 as generators say the approvals single-window system has stalled, with no solar project approvals granted for nearly six months. Investors also flag escalating costs, including an 8% banking-charge notice and a looming mandate for battery storage (BESS) on all new projects from April, which will push costs higher.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/9-devote: Nine members of one family were killed and six injured when their vehicle, carrying devotees returning from the Khatu Shyam temple, rammed a parked truck in Rajasthan's Kota; the injured were taken by ambulance to New Medical College Hospital for treatment.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Odisha's CM ordered a probe into foreign trips taken by former CM Naveen Patnaik and two officials, V K Pandian and Ravikant, during 2022-24, after RTI activists alleged the Japan and Italy trips had suspicious, opaque spending. Patnaik's BJD said it welcomes the inquiry while accusing the state's 'double-engine' government of using it to deflect from other issues; Patnaik reportedly made only two official foreign trips in 24 years as CM.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/t: Three cyclones, Arnab, Murasu and Akvan, formed over the Bay of Bengal within 23 days this year, an unusually high frequency against roughly 1.8 cyclones a year historically. Experts say as the monsoon withdraws, wind shear that normally suppresses cyclone formation weakens while sea waters stay warm, creating more favourable conditions for storms during the Bay's October-December season.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/education/bseb-clas: Bihar's school board (BSEB) released a second dummy admit card for Class 10 and 12 board exams in 2027; students can flag errors through a correction window open until November 26.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: India's Narcotics Control Bureau invoked rarely-used provisions of the NDPS Act, not applied in over a decade, to probe six Indians arrested for allegedly facilitating US drug transactions. The provisions let the agency act against people in India controlling drug trade conducted entirely abroad, carrying 10-20 years' imprisonment and fines up to Rs 2 lakh for violations, reflecting a tougher stance on cross-border trafficking networks.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Gokul Milk Union raised buffalo milk prices by Rs 6 and cow milk by Rs 4 per litre, citing drought conditions, with procurement rates to farmers also rising. Effective November 21 and reviewed monthly, farmers say the increase still doesn't cover their rising cattle feed and fodder costs, highlighting the squeeze on dairy supply chains during weak monsoons.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Kolhapur's Gokul Milk Union unanimously raised buffalo milk prices by Rs 6 and cow milk by Rs 4 per litre, with procurement rates to farmers up by Rs 3 and Rs 2 respectively, calling it a 'historic' hike amid drought. The new rates run roughly 131 days through March, reviewed monthly as milk supply is expected to decline across Maharashtra, though producers say it's still inadequate.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: California's Attorney General issued a subpoena in a probe examining whether Nvidia and former CEO Jensen Huang violated state civil and criminal laws by misleading investors about alleged chip sales to China despite US export restrictions. The investigation, still preliminary with no conclusions reached, adds legal risk for Nvidia after Huang stepped down on November 12 amid other controversies.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's GST Network added metro rail as a fifth transport mode in the e-way bill system, alongside road, rail, air and ship, following an October 26 government notification. Users moving goods via metro must now select this mode and enter transport document numbers, a small but practical compliance update for businesses using e-way bills.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: An analyst recommended three stocks under Rs 100, IDFC First Bank, Jayaswal Neco Industries and Sagility, as Indian markets rallied, with the Nifty 50 up 2.61% and Sensex up 2,300 points for the week, led by PSU banks. The Nifty cleared key resistance levels on a bullish chart pattern, though its RSI of 78 signals overbought conditions.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c680: A broad tech sell-off pushed the S&P 500 and Dow Jones into correction territory, down 10%+ from recent highs, as Anthropic's shares fell back toward their IPO price after a strong debut. The S&P 500 fell 3.7%, the Dow 1.9% and the Nasdaq 5.3% on Friday amid concerns over the pace and scale of AI investment, which has topped $1 trillion in the past year among a handful of big tech firms.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urged banks to increase lending to small businesses, saying its economic impact is far broader than loans to large companies. He also stressed promoting financial literacy, cautious digital banking use, and continuing financial-inclusion camps to close service gaps in underserved communities.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Hero FinCorp, the NBFC arm of Hero MotoCorp, aims to double its loan disbursements across northern India over the next two quarters, after disbursing over 480,000 loans to households and businesses across seven states between January and September. The push relies on its diversified retail, MSME and corporate lending portfolio and AI-led underwriting, as it looks to grow while maintaining customer trust.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Amazon is nearing a $7.5 billion deal to acquire AI startup Decart, whose software helps AI models run more efficiently on fewer chips, strengthening AWS's competition with Nvidia. Decart, valued at $4 billion in May, was an early adopter of Amazon's Trainium3 chip and had also held talks with Nvidia, one of its investors; a deal could close as soon as next week.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India and Finland are deepening economic ties through startup cooperation, with Finland's ambassador highlighting engagement with Indian startups to boost investment. The Polar Bear Pitching event showcased startups, with Yash Goliya's win earning a spot in a 2027 global competition, as bilateral trade between the two countries continues to grow.
items.https://inc42.com/features/indian-startu: India's startup IPO momentum is set to continue into 2026 after a record 2025, when 18 startups raised Rs 41,248 crore via public listings; 29 more have already filed IPO papers with SEBI and 25+ are in planning. Analysts expect 2026 to bring more scrutiny, as investors prioritise profitability and low cash burn over growth-at-any-cost, following SEBI reforms like simplified filings and flexible ESOP rules that fuelled last year's surge.
items.https://entrackr.com/report/weekly-fundi: Indian startups raised $290 million across 23 deals (6 growth-stage, 17 early-stage) in the week of November 16-21, up sharply from $31.3 million the prior week. Notable rounds included CRM startup Dreamteam's $53 million round, fashion retailer parent Nexon Omniverse's roughly $52 million Series E, and robotics firm Botsync's $11 million Series B, alongside several leadership appointments and two exits.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Karnataka's transport minister Byrathi Suresh said a final decision on bike taxis will follow discussion with the Advocate General, after a Supreme Court order; the government is considering regulations and restrictions rather than a blanket ban.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/budget-2027-indus: Industry body Bharat Web3 Association urged the finance ministry to cut the 1% TDS and 30% tax on crypto profits ahead of Budget 2027, arguing clearer rules would boost compliance and strengthen India's domestic Web3 platforms. The ask comes as crypto exchanges face banking disruptions, regulatory scrutiny and cybersecurity incidents exposing vulnerabilities across the industry.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/rooters-r: Gaming live-streaming platform Rooter more than doubled its FY26 revenue to Rs 170.4 crore from Rs 78.9 crore, while narrowing losses 40% to Rs 19.2 crore, as India's gaming industry expands beyond gameplay into streaming, esports and commerce. Founded in 2016, Rooter lets users stream titles like BGMI and Valorant and has added gaming-commerce revenue by selling in-game currency and gift cards.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Anthropic staffer Levent Alpoge claims to have solved the Riemann Hypothesis, a long-unsolved 'Holy Grail' math problem, with help from Claude, detailing the proof in a four-page explanation posted on his website.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg said he hopes an independent forum into the Bancroft ball-tampering article will provide answers, though he doesn't expect definitive ones, as former coach Darren Lehmann again denies knowing about the 2018 sandpaper plot.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/vid: Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds United beat Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge, their first win there in 27 years, lifting Leeds to sixth in the Premier League.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/i: India declared at 720/9 on Day 4 of the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington, the highest team total ever recorded in a Test in New Zealand, surpassing the hosts' own 715/6 from 2019. Rishabh Pant's 128 off 153 balls, including 10 fours and six sixes, headlined a morning session in which India added 143 runs, building a lead beyond 260 before declaring.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: England face a captaincy dilemma after deputy Jacks suffered a hand injury that could rule him out for the rest of the tour, including the final match he had been set to captain.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/vid: Noni Madueke's second-half goal earned Arsenal a 2-2 draw at Newcastle, keeping the reigning Premier League champions six points clear at the top of the table.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/s: Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann again denied knowing his players planned to use sandpaper on the ball during the 2018 Cape Town Test, saying the scandal took him to a 'dark place' mentally. He acknowledged resigning under pressure as coach at the time and said 'we all made mistakes,' speaking during cricket commentary roughly eight and a half years after the incident.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/21/signal: Messaging app Signal is restricting screenshots on Android and iOS, after already blocking them by default on Windows, calling OS-level agentic AI an 'existential threat' to privacy. President Meredith Whittaker said AI agents that can 'scan' screen content let sensitive chat data be captured and sent to outside servers beyond Signal's control; users can disable the feature, which Whittaker admits is only a partial fix.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/googl: Google rolled out a redesigned desktop search homepage that drops the dedicated search button and adds buttons for AI image generation, file analysis and Gemini brainstorming, after weeks of testing. The 'I'm Feeling Lucky' button stays, but the move reflects Google reshaping its core search product around AI chat features rather than traditional search.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI evaluation nonprofit METR updated its widely-cited 'time horizon' chart, which tracks how long a task frontier AI models can complete, measured by how long it takes humans, a length that had been doubling every four months. The updated version adds longer and more open-ended tasks and finds models are improving fast at coding but comparatively weaker at tasks requiring judgment, nuancing a chart that had often been misread.

MIT Technology Review's AI Hype Index notes AI's spread into nearly everything: Google's AI Overviews cost it billions in lost ad revenue even as it pushes them, AI-powered humanoid robots are appearing in daily chores, and an AI-assisted cyberattack reportedly caused a supermarket mishap, arguing that despite the ubiquity, a decade after AlphaGo, AI still falls short of some of the loftier claims made about it.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/21/all-th: TechCrunch rounded up notable AI agents that work by text message rather than an app, able to remember context, connect to other services, and handle tasks like scheduling, travel research, emails and reminders. The list highlights fast-growing players like Instinct, now valued at $10 billion after a $1 billion funding round, alongside assistants such as Proxy, built to anticipate users' needs.
items.https://www.theverge.com/games/1038099/c: Chess.com is launching a public beta of 'Classic Games,' adding 10 titles, including backgammon, checkers, go, mahjong, shogi, sudoku and a Scrabble alternative called Word, via web and new iOS/Android apps. The expansion follows Chess.com's earlier launch of Gambit, a gambling-free poker site, as the company diversifies beyond chess into other classic games with communities of their own.
items.https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11: A researcher planted 2 million trackable digital 'canaries' into prompts sent through AI router services like OpenRouter, which route requests to whichever inference provider is cheapest or best suited, to test whether sensitive data stays private. The experiment found the broker ecosystem leaked sensitive information, including AWS access keys, at an alarming rate, exposing privacy risks in the AI supply chain that sit outside the control of the original AI providers.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: AI startup Osmo, working with roughly 30 trained human 'sniffers' near Newark Airport, says it has built a foundation model for smell that founder Alex Wiltschko claims has reached 'human-level olfactory intelligence,' matching the average person's ability to detect and tell odors apart. The sniffers' descriptive notes are cross-referenced with chemical analysis to train the model, with Wiltschko framing scent as one of the oldest, most universal forms of communication.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/21/a-tale: TechCrunch's Equity podcast contrasts Nvidia's strong latest earnings report with growing pressure from tech executives, including Elon Musk, pushing for ousted CEO Jensen Huang's return via a petition. Despite reassurances from current leadership that growth will continue, Nvidia's falling stock price suggests investors aren't fully convinced, highlighting lingering uncertainty after Huang's exit.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/meta-: Meta is reconsidering its 2030 net-zero emissions goal after its latest sustainability report showed the largest percentage rise in greenhouse gas emissions among major Big Tech firms building AI data centers. Executives said AI infrastructure demand has grown faster than almost anyone projected, prompting a review of timelines and interim targets, a sign other tech giants racing to build AI capacity may face similar pressure to walk back climate commitments.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: A petition to reinstate ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang drew over 115,000 signatures, including Elon Musk and executives from Hugging Face and VC firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia, many with a stake in open-source AI, models that can be downloaded and run independent of big tech firms. Supporters argue Huang had become a champion for open models that let startups compete without paying large AI labs, raising questions about concentration of power in the AI industry.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/20/chips-: As companies explore building data centers in space, TechCrunch notes financing is a growing obstacle alongside engineering: data-center debt deals typically use chips as collateral that lenders can repossess on default, but that's impossible for chips orbiting Earth on a satellite. The report centers on SpaceX's $40 billion chip financing deal, where lenders are reportedly uneasy about collateral they can't physically reclaim, even though older chips like H100s and H200s still retain significant resale value.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/21/is-sel: Microdrama startup Shortical, known for bite-sized melodramatic romance series, has licensed actor Aki Avni's AI-generated likeness for its latest show, 'Inevitable,' a trend already popular in China. AI content costs far less to produce than live-action while offering similar or greater profit potential if it draws an audience, raising questions about whether licensing one's face to AI studios could become a new norm in Hollywood.
items.https://techcrunch.com/podcast/the-fallo: TechCrunch's Equity podcast discusses Nvidia's fallout from ousting CEO Jensen Huang alongside a strong earnings report showing healthy growth, with management insisting there are no plans to bring him back. Nvidia confirmed it will stop selling its H200 chips in China, a move discussed alongside Anthropic's recent IPO, seen as a test of the AI industry's circular funding model.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1039554/un: UN diplomats in Geneva failed to agree on binding rules for autonomous weapons ('killer robots'), settling only to 'start discussing options' after a largely fruitless week. The Red Cross and UN secretary-general had pushed for binding rules within a year, but countries agreed to a two-year compromise instead, with some future rules left optional, even as semi-autonomous weapons and drones have caused significant civilian deaths in conflicts including Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan.
items.https://www.theverge.com/policy/1038892/: President Trump threatened a 'tremendous tax' on US companies that build AI data centers outside the country, warning that doing so would let China 'take them all,' even as many US states and cities impose new restrictions on data center construction. Trump compared the risk to past offshoring of chip manufacturing, which he said hurt the US, but offered no details on how such a tax would work.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: Four Black high schoolers in Baltimore County are suing their school and police after an AI gun-detection system flagged one student holding a bag of Doritos as a potential gunman in 2025. Though officials cleared the false alert within two minutes via camera footage, police were still called and responded with multiple patrol cars; the lawsuit cites a system where over 99% of alerts were false positives.
items.https://www.theverge.com/podcast/1038701: The Verge's AI-in-real-life podcast series closes by examining whether Anthropic can keep prioritizing AI safety now that it's a public company on the Nasdaq facing shareholder pressure and roughly $900 billion in projected compute costs. The episode frames the IPO as a test of whether Anthropic's safety-first mission can coexist with the commercial demands of being one of the most valuable companies in the world.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/bewakoof-cofounde: Bewakoof cofounder Prabhkiran Singh has launched Save8, an AI shopping assistant that compares prices and offers across more than 1,000 e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms, marking his return to entrepreneurship after exiting the fashion brand he led for 14 years. Singh is in early fundraising talks with investors including All In Capital, though the funding amount and final investor lineup remain undisclosed.
items.https://inc42.com/features/sarvams-token: Sarvam AI launched a commercial 'Token Factory' letting developers access multiple AI models via API and pay per token used, without managing their own GPU infrastructure, joining rivals like L&T, Jarvislabs, Utho Labs and Mirror Security in India's emerging AI inference-as-a-service market. The move reflects Indian infrastructure players shifting from simple GPU rentals toward managed, token-based services as domestic AI adoption drives inference demand.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/scaler-cofounder-: Scaler cofounder Anshuman Singh has launched Arcfront with Naman Bhalla to commercialize records of expert professional decision-making as training and testing data for AI models on judgment-heavy tasks, claiming four of the five frontier AI labs became customers within a year, though he didn't name them.
